questions.stem: Under the Small Vessel Regulations, which description fits a "workboat"?
options: Any vessel not carrying passengers, not human-powered and not a pleasure craft
Any vessel that earns money, including commercial fishing boats
Any vessel under 8 m in length that tows another vessel
A vessel of 15 GT or less that carries fewer than 12 passengers
questions.explanation: The definition works by exclusion (s. 1). Fishing vessels are not workboats for this purpose because the Regulations do not apply to them at all (s. 2). Towing is not part of the definition, and a boat that carries passengers is a passenger-carrying vessel, not a workboat.

questions.stem: A 12 m commercial fishing boat of 9 GT asks which SVR workboat equipment table applies to her. What is the correct answer?
options: Part 5, because she is under 15 gross tonnage
Part 4, because she carries a crew of more than one
Part 5 for equipment but Part 7 for construction
None, as the SVR do not apply to fishing vessels
questions.explanation: Section 2(2)(a) excludes fishing vessels from the Small Vessel Regulations. Her size and crew do not bring her back in. Other regulations deal with fishing vessels.

questions.stem: A company buys a 7 m work skiff to haul tools and materials to a float camp and plans to start next Monday. What must the owner do under Part 5 before the skiff is first put into service?
options: Obtain an inspection certificate from a marine safety inspector
File a compliance notice with the Minister before the first working trip
Tell the Minister of the intended operation and the boat's details
Nothing, because the duty falls only on the operator at sea
questions.explanation: Section 502 puts an informing duty on the owner before first service. An inspection certificate is a Vessel Safety Certificates Regulations matter for larger vessels, and the compliance notice is a plate fixed to the vessel, not a filing. The Minister may also ask for the information later (s. 503).

questions.stem: A 10.5 m workboat has a freeboard so that the climb to reboard is 0.4 m. Which throwing gear and reboarding equipment does Part 5 require?
options: A 15 m buoyant heaving line only, and a reboarding device
A heaving line and a lifebuoy on a line, but no reboarding device
A lifebuoy on a 15 m line only, and no reboarding device
Both a heaving line and a lifebuoy, plus a reboarding device
questions.explanation: Over 9 m and up to 12 m the table requires both items (s. 506). A reboarding device is needed unless the vertical climb is 0.5 m or less, and 0.4 m qualifies for the exception. The "line only" and "lifebuoy only" answers belong to the shorter length bands.

questions.stem: Which set of visual signals must a 7.5 m workboat carry?
options: Watertight flashlight and 6 pyrotechnic distress signals other than smoke
Watertight flashlight and 3 pyrotechnic distress signals other than smoke
Watertight flashlight and 12 pyrotechnic distress signals, not more than 6 of them smoke
Pyrotechnic distress signals only, as a flashlight is not required
questions.explanation: Over 6 m and up to 9 m the table calls for a flashlight and six non-smoke signals (s. 507). Three is the figure to 6 m and twelve (up to six smoke) is the figure over 9 m. The flashlight is required in every band.

questions.stem: Two boats, each 9 m long with two people aboard, are working in BC waters. One is a workboat that is not a tug; the other is a tug. Which statement about life rafts is correct?
options: Both must carry a life raft big enough for two people
Neither must carry one, because the trigger for both is over 12 m
Only the workboat, because tugs are covered by Part 6, not Part 5
Only the tug, as a tug over 8.5 m with two aboard needs a raft
questions.explanation: Section 508 triggers for a workboat over 12 m. Section 509 sets a lower trigger for a tug over 8.5 m with two or more persons aboard. The tug is still a workboat covered by Part 5; tugs fall under Part 6 for the stability and strength duty, not instead of Part 5.

questions.stem: An 11 m workboat carries an anchor with 25 m of cable and a manual bilge pump. What is wrong, if anything?
options: Nothing, because an anchor is optional if there is a bilge pump
She needs 50 m because all workboats over 9 m need 50 m
The rode is too short: over 9 m to 12 m needs at least 30 m
She needs a bailer instead of a manual bilge pump
questions.explanation: The table in s. 510 gives 15 m (to 9 m, where a manual propelling device is an alternative), 30 m (over 9 m to 12 m) and 50 m (over 12 m). The pump is correct for her band. A bailer is only an option in the smallest band.

questions.stem: A 10 m open workboat begins towing. Which arrangement is required by the towing rules for workboats?
options: A single lifejacket in the wheelhouse and the tow line made fast to the stern cleat
A way to release or cut the tow line at once, and a clear deck aft of the tow point
A tow line fixed with no release, so that it cannot part under load
An extra life raft on board whatever the length of the boat
questions.explanation: Section 521 requires immediate release or cutting of the tow line, a clear deck aft of the towing point so the line can swing, two lifejackets in the wheelhouse, two means of escape from the wheelhouse, and (for an open boat) positive buoyancy when swamped or a high gunwale. A fixed stern-cleat tow is the setup that causes girding.

questions.stem: The owner of a 7.2 m tug asks whether she needs a compliance notice under Part 8 and whether the Part 7 construction requirements apply. What is the correct answer?
options: Neither: Parts 7 and 8 exclude tugs, and Part 6 applies instead
A notice is required but Part 7 does not apply to her
A notice is required because she is over 6 m, and Part 7 applies
Neither applies, because no part of the SVR covers tugs
questions.explanation: Section 700(4) excludes tugs from Part 7 and s. 800(2) excludes them from Part 8. Part 6 applies to vessels that Part 7 does not (s. 600), and Part 5 covers her equipment. The idea that no part of the SVR covers tugs is wrong, because Parts 5 and 6 do.

questions.stem: When the loading of a small cargo-carrying workboat is questioned, who has a legal duty under s. 601(2) to ensure she has adequate stability and structural strength for her intended operations?
options: The owner only, as the operator follows orders
The operator only, as the person at the helm
The builder only, through the compliance notice
Both the owner and the operator of the vessel
questions.explanation: Section 601(2) names both the owner and the operator and applies to vessels other than pleasure craft. Builders have their own duties in Part 7, but this duty is not theirs alone.

questions.stem: A 14 m non-pleasure workboat gets a new deckhouse and a heavier crane that change her stability. What must the owner do?
options: Nothing, because only pleasure craft are affected by modifications
Re-certify the vessel under the Vessel Safety Certificates Regulations in every case
Meet the construction rules in force when work began, and tell the Minister
Wait for the Minister to request the stability data before doing anything
questions.explanation: A modification that affects stability or watertight integrity is a major modification (s. 710). It must meet the construction requirements in force when the work started, and the owner of a non-pleasure vessel must inform the Minister. Separately, stability must be adequate and the owner must demonstrate it on request (s. 716), but that does not make the informing duty wait for a request.

questions.stem: A 5.4 m non-pleasure workboat carries a compliance notice. What does the notice for a vessel of 6 m or less state in addition to the construction statement?
options: The name of the last inspector and the date of the last inspection done
The maximum safe load and persons and, for outboards, maximum power
The registration number and port of registry of the vessel
The water temperature below which a life raft must be carried
questions.explanation: Section 802(1)(g) requires these recommended maximum safe limits for vessels of 6 m or less. The notice is a plate or label fixed where it is visible from the operating position (s. 801(6)), and it must be in English and French. It is not an inspection record or a registry document.

questions.stem: A 14 GT vessel carries 20 passengers on a day tour. Which regime applies to her?
options: The VSCR: she must hold a safety certificate to make the voyage
The Small Vessel Regulations, Part 5, as a workboat
The Small Vessel Regulations, Part 4, as a passenger vessel
No regime applies, because she is under 15 GT
questions.explanation: Division 2 of the Vessel Safety Certificates Regulations covers vessels of 15 GT or less that carry more than 12 passengers, as well as every vessel over 15 GT (s. 11). Part 4 of the SVR covers up to 12 passengers, and Part 5 is for workboats, which do not carry passengers.
